messages:
Maria: quick follow-up from the compaction RFC thread — thinking about a soft-compact mode that favors liveness over max packing. want feedback on heuristics and an escape hatch.
AJ: curious — can you sketch what "soft-compact" actually does at enqueue time vs eviction time?
Maria: yeah. idea: instead of force-merging small windows every cycle, we'd allow small windows to persist for X ms unless headroom drops below a threshold. this avoids starving long-tail low-qps tenants.
Devon: so we keep more live small windows, tradeoffs are memory + slightly lower batch utilization, but better p99 for those tenants, right?
Maria: exactly. and to keep costs bounded, compaction runs with a backoff proportional to global memory pressure.
Sam: can we make it tenant-configurable? some customers want max cost predictability.
Maria: yes — propose config keys:
```yaml
soft_compact.enabled: true
soft_compact.max_delay_ms: 50
soft_compact.memory_pressure_pct: 80
soft_compact.tenant_override: false
```
AJ: two concerns: 1) how does this interact with KV-cache eviction? if we keep windows longer we hold more KV state per tenant. 2) fairness — a noisy tenant could abuse soft windows to pin resources.
Kevin: for (1) we should wire a kvcache-priority signal into the compactor so if a tenant's KV share exceeds threshold we compact regardless.
Devon: for (2) consider a token-bucket per tenant that charges for live-window millis. noisy tenants deplete quickly and compactor prioritizes their windows. that preserves fairness without global hard blocks.
Maria: good call. token-bucket idea seems nice and easy to reason about. metric to track: live_window_ms_per_minute per tenant.
Infra-bot: experiment deployed to canary-5: soft-compact.enabled=true, max_delay_ms=30, memory_pressure_pct=85.
Sam: what observability do we need? i want per-route cost delta and p50/p99 before/after, plus live_window_ms histogram.
Maria: yep: add these to the rollout dashboard and a regression alert if a tenant's token-bucket refill rate is exhausted -> sustained >5s.
AJ: nit: make the default max_delay small (20-50ms). longer values hide batching artifacts and can make latency SLOs ambiguous.
Devon: also add a debug endpoint that lists live windows and their sizes for a tenant id — useful during incident triage.
Maria: agree. final open Q: should soft-compact be on by default for hosted API? my gut: turned off for low-tier customers and on for higher tiers, since higher tiers value latency consistency more. thoughts?
Sam: defaults based on tier seems sensible. we can also auto-disable if cost goes >10% on a tenant.
Kevin: implement escape hatch: admin API flag to force hard-compact per host or tenant. emergency kill switch.
Maria: thanks all — will draft follow-up RFC with config names, token-bucket math, and a small canary plan. if anyone wants to pair on the metric set, ping me. :rocket:
AJ: sounds good. +1 to token-bucket and escape hatch.
Devon: i'll take the debug endpoint.
Sam: i'll add dashboard panels for rollout.
Infra-bot: canary metrics posted to #deployments/canary-5: https://deploys.redwood.example/canary-5/6832123456
Maria: moving to implement, will update RFC.
